svg.text: Pi drawn to scale from above; Bonnet laid out from Adafruit's photo; panel not to scale. Red = 5 V, black = ground.
the Bonnet plugs onto the 40-pin header, inside the yellow outline
LED panel, back (64x64 shown; a 64x32 is half as tall)
arrows on the back point away from IN
panel power lead, into the screw terminal
powers the panel and, through the
Bonnet, the Pi: the Pi needs no cable
Inside, a cut-off DC cord: its centre wire (+, red) to the
big tab with the centre pin, its other wire (−) to the sleeve
tab; the third (×, a switch) stays empty. The small tabs look
alike: with the supply in, the sleeve reads 5 V to the big tab.
Sound, option A (recommended): a USB speaker
power and sound over the one USB cable
Option B, instead of A: a small speaker built into the case
Some soldering; most likely to pick up buzz from the panel. Details in SOUND.md.
from the Bonnet's 5V screw terminal (+ and −)
One speaker, two channels: wire only the tip and mix left and right in ALSA (SOUND.md, Mono).
Power button: four wires to the Bonnet's breakout pads
The row under the header, labelled as on the Bonnet. A pad with a signal printed under it (OE, CLK, R1…)
is the Bonnet's own: don't solder to it. The rest are the Pi's free pins.
16 mm momentary button, green LED ring (Adafruit 560)
Unlabelled numbers are GPIO numbers. MO, MI, CLK, CE0, CE1 are the Pi's SPI pins (free here; this CLK isn't the panel's).
Keep I2C off (no dtparam=i2c_arm=on): SCL is GPIO 3, the button's pin.
The only pin a shut-down Pi still watches, so one button does both.
On while Linux runs, off when shutdown has finished. Any free pad would do.
The switch's and the LED's ground wires share it; every ground on the Pi is the same.
A wire between them, for smoother dim colours with adafruit-hat-pwm.
